It holds only that nothing in the coupling makes that form a subject, which [ADR-024](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-024.md) reserves "self" for. Open: whether that is the sense of "self" worth asking about is itself in question. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-166](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-166.md) v2 | A lower-level collective within the composite person, such as the gut microbiome, can at times drive higher-level behaviour and even experience: the routes exist and the effects are causal in rodents, while the human evidence is modest | The owner's thesis of 2026-10-11: "'who drives' isn't a constant. The time claim is filed as the owner's. The microbiome claim is grounded in two reviews read the same day. The routes exist, and the effects are causal in rodents. The human evidence is modest: associations, small effects on subjective stress, and nulls. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-167](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-167.md) | One-way drive rightly passes the threshold criterion: a metronome and its musician, or a nerve and its muscle, form one system relative to a target that needs both, and the direction of coupling gives the system's internal architecture, not its membership | The owner's challenge to the open objection, 2026-10-11: "a metronome driving a musician, or a nerve driving a muscle, passes — and why shouldn't they?" Three reasons, set out by the assistant and accepted for filing by the owner. Second, its intuitions are about agency, which [QUESTION-035](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md) keeps apart. Third, whether a one-way driver is inside the block or an input is a choice relative to the target. Direction tells peers from hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-168](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-168.md) | Identifying agents by their will-organization is circular: will-organization is defined for an agent already given, and the agent-versus-device comparison presupposes an identified system, so neither can produce the factorization it is meant to find | The record's anticipated objection to the owner's thesis. [TERM-023](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-023.md) is "agent-indexed": a role in an agent already warranted. The will paper supposes its agent ([CLAIM-080](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-080.md)) so as not to face [CLAIM-010](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-010.md). Orseau et al.'s formal agent-device comparison likewise "assume[s] a clearly identified system". To identify agents by will-organization reverses an order of explanation that was chosen deliberately. Open: [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md) replies that the test is run on candidate factors, not on agents. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-169](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-169.md) v2 | On Ainslie's account the population of interests is produced by desynchronized valuation, not given by a fixed architecture: an agent is many interests over a choice only as far as its valuations of that choice cross within the choice's horizon | The record's reading of [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md), made in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11. The self's intertemporal multiplicity is then a variable, not a constant. It does not say that all multiplicity of self is intertemporal. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-170](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-170.md) v4 | The agents in a system are a factorization of it relative to a level of description and a target; agents in general are identified by adaptation, and willed agents are individuated by their will-organization: a willed agent is the jurisdiction of a will-organization | The owner's thesis of 2026-10-11, stated in the record's terms after discussion. In the discussion, the owner chose will-organization over operative will, in the form "jurisdiction of a will-organization". Operative will flickers with the drive profile; a will-organization is maintained. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-171](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-171.md) | A stored text means only what its readings make of it: the writer's projected receiver is one more reading, so an unread text has possible meanings and no fixed one | The record's anticipated reception-side objection to the owner's storage claim. Open: the reply (the joke changed for the reader, not in what it was made to do) works only if the writer's frame is itself recoverable, and that is [QUESTION-031](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md)'s problem. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md) v7 | A candidate factor is an agent at a level when it is one system there, when a goal-directed description beats a device description by more than the Occam cost, and when its policy would adapt if its actions' consequences changed; it is a willed agent when, further, a will-organization over several regimes describes it better than none, and what passes that is the jurisdiction of a will-organization | The assistant's admission test for the owner's thesis, filed at the owner's request. It has three tests on a candidate factor, at a level and for a target. (1) System: it clears the threshold criterion. (2) Description: a model in which it governs its own regimes for goals beats a device model by more than the Occam cost (Orseau et al., priced as in [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md)). (3) Adaptation: its governance would change if its actions' consequences changed (Kenton et al.). It answers the circularity objection by running on candidates whose boundaries come from (1), not from agency, and it answers the permissiveness objection without the will paper's supposition. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-176](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-176.md) v4 | Recurrence is the trigger of persistence this record is built around: coding a thing the second time it turns up captures exactly the drift that defeats an argument, and keeps capture from flooding the record | The filing rule of [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) ("a thing gets a code the second time it turns up"), read as one trigger of persistence ([CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md)), and the one this record is built around. Narrowed to that on 2026-10-11, on the owner's reframing. The same threshold appears in three places in luria and was found independently each time. Proposed: the rule has been applied, but no other threshold has been compared with it. | Proposed |

The evidence is the two "crystallized arguments" of the What Survives Translation? exchange and the manuscripts drafted from them (workbench 2026/10/09/025539, 2026/10/10/040457). Proposed: the record is kept beside the manuscript, and nothing generates a manuscript from it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-179](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-179.md) v3 | When an agent does the filing, the cost of capturing argument falls on the party that would otherwise pay to re-derive it, which removes the disparity that design-rationale systems were abandoned over | The answer to the cautionary literature the owner filed before the argument schemes were built ([ADR-030](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-030.md)): design rationale goes uncaptured because whoever captures it is not whoever benefits. Proposed: the record has run for one week. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-180](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-180.md) v4 | Drift is retrieval failure outside a critical distance: a restatement close enough to an idea retrieves it, one that has drifted too far is taken for new, and a code bypasses retrieval by content altogether | Proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11, when the owner raised sparse distributed memory and Hebbian learning after [CLAIM-182](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-182.md), and filed at the owner's request. It reads the drift of [CLAIM-177](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) through SDM's critical distance (read in [NOTE-242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-242.md)) and Hopfield's basins of attraction (unread when filed; read 2026-10-14 in NOTE-819). The analogy is the claim; whether restatement distance predicts re-derivation has not been measured. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md) v7 | The record fixes the grammar an argument is expressed in, though not its shape: its closed vocabulary of schemes, roles and relations formalizes early, and a move that fits no CLAIM, TERM, ARG or declared relation is forced into one or lost until the misfit is noticed and the grammar amended to hold it | Shipman and Marshall's objection to formal representation ([LIT-756](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-756.md)), turned on this record, and narrowed on the owner's correction of 2026-10-11. | [CLAIM-182](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-182.md) v2 | Storage is not anchoring, addressability is: a structure that is kept but cannot be pointed at part by part does not stop re-derivation, and the same content becomes an anchor once its parts get addresses | An answer to [QUESTION-038](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-038.md), proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11 and filed at the owner's request. | [CLAIM-183](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-183.md) v4 | Generated views of the record, fed back into the exchange, become instruments of the argument: they show where its terms evolved faster than its formalism | From U40 of the translation exchange, the first time a generated view went back into the conversation (workbench 2026/10/10/040455). The assistant read the term-revisions chain as evidence about the manuscript, and made five moves in reply. One of them was "Nucleation itself is a case study". One instance, so Proposed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-184](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-184.md) v4 | Anchors entrench: a structure that persists early can lock in its framing, so that later structure grows on it and alternatives become hard to reach, and retirement by status is the record's remedy only if superseded anchors stop attracting new structure | The cost side of the owner's reframing ([CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md)), proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11 and filed at the owner's request. If persistence is what lets structure grow, it also lets early framings grow structure that is costly to undo. The test, whether Superseded entries keep drawing new citations, was run on 2026-11-06: they do not (note of that date). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md) v3 | The nucleation threshold of an argument is whatever makes a structure persist: a persistent structure is available as an anchor, and more complex structure can evolve only on anchors | The owner's reframing of 2026-10-11, after two readings showed that no physical nucleation threshold is a count. The threshold is not recurrence as such but whatever triggers persistence. Recurrence is the trigger this record is built around ([CLAIM-176](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-176.md)), and there are others. | [CLAIM-186](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-186.md) v4 | How fast an argument grows sets how it grows: drift tracks how fast new material arrives relative to how fast it is anchored, so a fast, prolific exchange branches, as a crystal grown far from equilibrium does, and a project memory stabilizes an argument by keeping anchoring up with arrival | Proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11, while correcting its own crystal analogy ([CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md)), and filed at the owner's request rather than on a second occurrence. The analogy is to morphological instability. Near equilibrium a growing crystal faces over, and far from it the faces branch. The evidence so far is anecdotal. The fastest stretch of the translation exchange carried two moves of thesis, and drift has not been measured against pace. There is no slow exchange to compare it with, so the claim is Proposed and untested. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-187](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-187.md) v2 | Whether two systems compute the same way can be tested by quotienting the full admissible symmetry group and measuring what remains: a residual barrier marks a different mechanism, and a feature with no counterpart blocks the comparison | The record's one fully measured case of "factor out the admissible symmetries, then test what survives", which the pragmatic-transport line's questions about invariants under admissible transformation ([QUESTION-027](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-027.md), [QUESTION-029](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-029.md), [QUESTION-036](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-036.md)) ask for in the abstract. | [CLAIM-189](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md) v3 | Fidelity is the wrong measure of a developing argument: maturing drops and changes things legitimately, so what a record can secure is traceability, change that is announced and located, not preservation | The counter to [CLAIM-191](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-191.md), filed with it. A developing argument aims at maturing, and [TERM-052](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-052.md) says maturing drops things legitimately. A fidelity profile would score legitimate dissolution as distortion. What the record secures is that change is announced and located: traceability. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-191](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-191.md) v2 | Restating an argument across memoryless sessions is iterated transport with only a weak channel back to the source: without anchors, restatements drift toward the collaborators' own framings rather than at random, and a code restores continuity of transmission | The first claim joining the nucleating-argument and pragmatic-transport lines, which shared no edges. A sequence of memoryless sessions restating an argument is a chain of retellings, the telephone game of [CASE-015](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-015.md). The transport line's results then predict that drift has a direction, toward the transmitters' prior ([THEORY-155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md), [CLAIM-090](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-090.md)), and that convergence is not preservation ([CLAIM-081](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-081.md)). A code supplies [CLAIM-002](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md)'s continuity of transmission. Proposed from a synthesis review; the counter is [CLAIM-189](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-192](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-192.md) v2 | A multi-session argument's thesis can move without any participant arguing for the move, which is a case of an organized whole's course coming apart from its members' intentions | Links the nucleating-argument line to the distributed-agency line. Proposed from the synthesis review; the owner's memory and veto are the main reason to doubt it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-193](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-193.md) v4 | A linear probe family can tell apart only realizations whose representations differ in normalized kernel, and kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed: any distinction beyond that is supplied by the analyst | A partial answer to [QUESTION-031](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md) for the linear case, from THEORYs the record held without linking them to the line. What a regularized linear readout decodes is a function of the normalized kernel ([THEORY-008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)); kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed (THEORY-004, THEORY-723); an inner product beyond that is a stipulation ([THEORY-018](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-018.md)); and spectral degeneracy does not identify the symmetry ([THEORY-019](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md)). Proved results for learned representations; the carry-over to communicative realizations is the filer's. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md) | A person's roles in contexts that do not meet cannot contradict one another: role conflict needs an overlap, which segregating audiences prevents and collapsed contexts create | The MoM manuscript models a person's roles ("daughter", "teacher", "friend") as sections over family, professional and social contexts, with identity as their global section, failing when the roles contradict. Roles in contexts that do not meet glue ([CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md)), so contradiction between them is not yet a failure. Conflict needs an overlap: an occasion on which two audiences are present at once. People manage the cover. They segregate audiences, which keeps the contexts disjoint, and they script the occasions where audiences must meet. Broadcast and networked media collapse contexts, which creates overlaps the person did not choose (boyd 2008, after Meyrowitz 1985). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-198](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-198.md) | Preference reversal is not yet disunity: interests that govern a choice at disjoint times glue, and a self is divided over a choice only on an overlap, which the agent's prediction of its own later valuation creates | Take an agent's interests as sections over contexts of choice, each governing the windows of time in which its valuation ranks first. If the windows do not overlap, the sections glue ([CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md)): someone who prefers the diet in the morning and the cake at night is a time-indexed preference, not a divided self. Division needs an overlap, a choice on which both interests bear at once. On Ainslie's account that overlap is made by recursive self-prediction: the present choice is valued as a forecast of the later ones, so the later interest's valuation enters the present context. That is where intertemporal bargaining happens, and it is the coupling [CLAIM-163](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md) found missing. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) | Over a fixed scenario, a change of global compatibility at small local distortion needs contextual judgements, which the behavioural data read so far lack; the form of the headline those data leave open is a change of cover, in which a rendering makes some of the source's questions undecidable for its readers and decides others the source left open | The record's narrowing, on 2026-10-10, of [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md) after [CLAIM-219](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-219.md). It concedes that the record's reading of [LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md) finds no contextual behavioural data, so the fixed-scenario form of "Translation may preserve local meanings while changing the global structure of meaning" has no case but a constructed one. It shows why the fixed-scenario form is sharp and why it needs contextuality. It keeps the form the record already names: "Only a change of scenario can make it jump" ([CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md)), and manuscript §11's "A transport may preserve overlaps but change the available measurement cover". A proposal; its test is the discriminating study. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-202](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-202.md) v2 | What the line adds to functional and relevance-theoretic accounts of translation is measured structure beyond a static pragmatic profile: the context-indexed profile, its response to later framings and its decision relevance predict receivers' recovery beyond the similarity of static stance and footing ratings | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md). A proposal, untested. It does not say the functionalist rivals are wrong. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-204](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md) v3 | A communicative kind's identity is grounded in its relational organization, for which competent participants' uptake is the standard; statistical methods recover aspects of it from restricted observations; translation transports it; and what persists is what the receivers can still recover, of which the analyst can certify the independently identifiable part | The record's restatement, on 2026-10-10, of [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) after the audit's objections to it ([CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md), [CLAIM-232](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md), [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md), [CLAIM-206](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md), [CLAIM-222](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md), [CLAIM-246](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-246.md), [CLAIM-211](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-211.md)). It keeps the four clauses, adds [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md)'s standard to the first and [CLAIM-223](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-223.md)'s reading to the fourth, and replaces the third defeat disjunct ("no relational structure beyond the observed response profiles is needed", which [CLAIM-206](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md) showed is always met or undecidable) with an observable comparison on transfer. It supersedes [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md), by the owner's delegated ruling of 2026-10-29. A proposal, not a finding. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-206](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md) | If a communicative kind can outrun every probe, human same-kind judgements, themselves one probe family, can neither confirm nor defeat the October thesis; if it cannot, the kind does in the tests only what an observational class does, which the record's term for a kind says it is not | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens, with one point from the empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. It does not say kinds are unreal, and it is not [CLAIM-150](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-150.md)'s underdetermination of the ontology. | Proposed |

| [CLAIM-212](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-212.md) v3 | Fidelity as a report and fidelity as a re-performance are different decision targets: Blackwell's order compares a rendering with its source as evidence about the source's situation, which both readers decide about, while a rendering that re-performs the act in the target's situation is compared only through a correspondence of situations | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-258](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md), which it reconciles rather than refutes. A proposal; it does not say which kind of fidelity literary translation aims at. | Proposed |

Proposed and not adopted. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-215](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-215.md) v2 | Communicative kinds are repeatable organizations of relations among participants, norms, commitments and possible consequences, which concrete events realize without being one another, and which kind an event realizes is not exhausted by the intrinsic properties of the expression token | The assistant's first thesis at U62 (A240 T1; A232's first proposition and §2), which splits the ontological clause of the October thesis ([CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)) out from the rest and narrows it. | [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md) v2 | For a communicative kind, the standard of sufficiency is the uptake of competent participants who know the standings and norms in play: a defeasible standard, overridden only where the act's other constituents diverge from the judges' verdicts, so a probe family is tested against it, and a kind outruns the families coarser than that standard and the judges only through those constituents | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-206](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md), and the argument [CLAIM-247](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-247.md) found missing. Calling a probe family insufficient ([CLAIM-142](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md), [CLAIM-135](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-135.md)) presupposes a standard beyond it. For an act partly constituted by uptake ([CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md)), competent participants' uptake is that standard, and since version 2 a defeasible one: CLAIM-241 is conceded, so the verdicts yield where the act's other constituents diverge from them. The kind's extension is the class the standard fixes, and analysts' families are insufficient when coarser. No test needs a kind that outruns every family. A proposal, resting on a Proposed premise. It does not touch [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)'s ontological clause, which the programme does not test. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-220](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-220.md) v2 | For a named population of receivers and a stated family of tasks, what survives a translation, retelling or rendering is the set of task-relevant communicative distinctions those receivers can still recover from it, and measured preservation of the pragmatic observables predicts that recovery better than preservation of the wording or of the proposition, with or without its force | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to the audit's objections to the tests of the manuscript's thesis ([CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md), [CLAIM-232](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md), [CLAIM-243](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-243.md), [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md), [CLAIM-226](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-226.md), [CLAIM-222](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md)). It restates [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) as an empirical claim indexed to receivers and tasks, tested against the rival [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) itself names, a proposition with its force, on a behavioural criterion and with an interlingual arm that decides. It supersedes [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md), by the owner's delegated ruling of 2026-10-29. It is a proposal, not a finding. It does not claim the line's distinctive machinery is needed: that is [CLAIM-202](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-202.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-221](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-221.md) v2 | The relational-constitution thesis's defeat condition describes a standard rival the record holds no counter for, intention-based accounts of illocution, which plausibly meet it for every act in the four-speakers case except the institutional one | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) is defeated by a held account that individuates teasing, reproach and reprimand by the utterance plus speaker-internal states. That is the intention-based line of Grice, Strawson and Bach and Harnish, none of whom the record holds. On it [CASE-018](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-018.md)'s friend, parent and comedian differ in communicative intention, and only the judge needs norms, which Searle ([LIT-482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-482.md)) already supplies. The record's own model for [CLAIM-111](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-111.md) is of this family. The objection is open; it would narrow [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) to institutional acts unless an argument from uptake meets it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-224](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-224.md) | Under partial relational constitution, a translation always changes the participants, audience and norms that the relational-constitution thesis makes constituents of the act, so whether the act survives turns on a correspondence of relations the structure cannot supply from inside | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. That makes [QUESTION-005](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md) a question about what the act is, not only how to measure it, and the record's model of translation holds the audience fixed. [CLAIM-138](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-138.md) spares [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md); this applies its point to [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) through translation. The objection is open. It does not say acts never survive translation. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md) v4 | D_obs restated over a rendering procedure, with one kernel family fitted on some source items and scored on held-out ones and the target term the readers' response averaged over the procedure's output, separates rendering procedures that receivers' task-indexed recovery separates, so restated it measures observational fidelity informatively | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, of the manuscript's L_obs and the profile's D_obs after [CLAIM-207](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md), [CLAIM-230](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md) and [CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md). For one pair a constant kernel makes D_obs zero ([CLAIM-207](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md)); fixed across items, it fits only if the target readers' responses do not vary with the item. The repair ties the outcome-level kernels to the text channel, makes the transport a property of a procedure ([CLAIM-230](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md)), and makes deficiency a finite computation over judgement outcomes ([CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md)). A proposal: the derivation is elementary, but whether the restated measure is informative is the defeat condition's empirical question. It does not say a fitted kernel is the translator's process. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-240](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-240.md) v3 | A holistic fidelity judgement is fidelity under the judges' default task, a weighting of the profile's components that can be estimated on some renderings and tested on others, so it is well defined and consistent with task-relativity, and a defeat condition that uses it must name the population and fix the weighting before the test, and across populations with unequal access to the source must fit the weighting only on the components each can perceive | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md). Task-relativity ([CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md)) denies a ranking that holds across tasks, not that a population has a default task. A weighting estimated on held-in data and tested on held-out data is a finding, not a fit, and a weighting fixed before the test leaves no room to blame the task after a failure. A proposal: whether holistic judgements are such a weighting is itself empirical. The objection is right that the stated defeat conditions name neither task nor receivers; [CLAIM-220](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-220.md), [CLAIM-204](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md) and [QUESTION-075](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-075.md) address that. | Proposed |

It grants the objection's premises: value is internal to one language state, and it is a fact of langue, while the line's observables are facts of use. It denies the conclusion. What the premise rules out is identity of value across languages, which the line does not claim ([CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)), and transport through a correspondence fixed from outside both systems is what [CLAIM-082](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-082.md)'s own qualification already requires. At the level of use, contrast with alternatives is the rational-speech-act model's premise ([THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md)) and Bergen, Goodman and Levy's finding ([LIT-809](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-809.md)). Saussure becomes precedent, not premise. A proposal, not a refutation. | Proposed |

The theory's measure must then be fitted to that weighting, which is circular, or a mismatch blamed on the judges' task, which leaves nothing that defeats. It does not say the judgements are useless, only that the defeat conditions lack the task and receiver index the line's own theses say fidelity needs. [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md) is its neighbour: that one moves the criterion to the analyst, and neither says it is task-free. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-250](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-250.md) v2 | What a developing argument should preserve through legitimate revision is its accountability structure, what was asserted, why, how it was challenged and what justified its revision, not its propositions, so fidelity is defined over justificatory and provenance relations while propositional content changes | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12, on the third open tension ([CLAIM-189](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md) against [CLAIM-252](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-252.md)). | [CLAIM-251](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-251.md) v2 | A change in which questions a receiver population can answer determinately is not by itself a change of cover in the sheaf sense: the cover belongs to the measurement scenario and the responses are an empirical model on it, so such a change is a change of empirical model, which can create or remove a gluing obstruction on a fixed cover but does not change what the cover is, and the operational notion needs its own name until a functorial link is shown | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12, on the open tension between [CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md) with [CASE-048](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-048.md) and the operational cover of [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md). It keeps the empirical notion and denies it the sheaf-theoretic name. Open. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-255](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-255.md) v2 | Intending to perform an act, performing it and being recognized as having performed it are distinct, coupled variables: intended meaning is fixed at production, the act partly by roles, standing and norms, and recognition by uptake, so competent uptake is constitutive for some acts, evidential for others and irrelevant to the existence of still others | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12, on the first open tension ([CLAIM-160](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-160.md) against [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) and [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md)). [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s comparison is over one state Z. It does not say decision-relative fidelity is wrong. | Proposed |

Twitch Plays Pokémon approximates one, best in democracy mode with the tally visible as votes arrive. Read a barrier that survives as a difference of mechanism ([THEORY-116](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-116.md)). Between linearly connected image classifiers, nearly every layer's features interpolate ([THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md)). | [CLAIM-271](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-271.md) v2 | A collective's reasons need not be any of its members' reasons, so aggregating members' conclusions, as polling does, can yield verdicts the collective's own reasons do not support | The owner's thesis of 2026-10-13, given in conversation by refining "the good of a higher level agent need not align with the respective goods of the parts" to reasons. So the "temperature" of random corruption is high early and low late. This is a feedback from pattern to flow, and it answers [QUESTION-085](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-085.md) in part. Untested on the logs. | Proposed |

It does not say coherence is bad. | Proposed |

Indexing grants by role, E_i(j, r, c, t), lets i back j as an error detector without backing j's authority over the final choice. Under them, empowering a better-placed ally is a way to get one's policies realized without becoming more powerful. It does not say such schemes resist collusion, or that alignment makes delegation wise. | Proposed |

| [CLAIM-295](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-295.md) v3 | A record of an inquiry's justifications adds nothing for decisions its current state already suffices for: what it can add is a wider family of decisions for which what is kept suffices, and decisions a bounded agent can make that it otherwise could not | A10's conclusion, with A5's second claim and A10 §5's three values of history: informational, computational and option value. [CLAIM-250](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-250.md) says what accountable inquiry ought to preserve; this says what preserving it could buy. The cases make the first half exact ([CLAIM-294](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-294.md), [CLAIM-300](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-300.md)). The second half, that real inquiries change their questions in ways that make the purchase worth its cost, is not shown. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-298](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md) v2 | A frame can change a judgement by changing which of an interpreter's stored distinctions are reachable, without supplying any evidence about what is being judged | A20's proposed claim, after the owner tied addressing to anchoring at U20, and A19's "addressing conditions". (2019, read) find the most direct measure of the accessibility step does not replicate and cannot detect priming at all. The retrieval step is inferred, not shown. The mechanism the record holds, attention as sparse distributed memory ([LIT-269](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md)), is a model, not evidence about judges. The extension to communication in general is the record's and is not shown. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-301](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-301.md) v2 | Iterative retrieval can turn a provisional interpretation into a premise: a framing selects what is encountered, what is encountered reinforces the framing, and the question being investigated drifts as well as the queries | A21's proposed claim, from the owner's U21 link between retrieval-mediated anchoring, agent harnesses and older information retrieval. Classical IR named query drift ([LIT-1079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1079.md)). An agent that rewrites its own task adds [TERM-056](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-056.md), which A21 judged "arguably more consequential". The exchange did this itself between A2 and A13. | Proposed |

A11's four expenditures (materialization, indexing, dependency tracking, refresh) and its break-even condition. The arithmetic is trivial. The thesis is about the record: that its second-occurrence rule ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)) and the nucleation threshold of [CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md) are approximations to this trade, and can fail in both directions. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-308](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md) v3 | Where reuse cannot be forecast, recurrence weighted by reconstruction cost is the filing criterion, not only evidence for one: filing at the first use at which reconstructing again would take the overpayment past the cost of filing is within 2 − (c_a + u)/c_r of the hindsight optimum on every sequence of uses, at most twice, and no deterministic rule without foresight guarantees materially better, under fixed known costs, with staleness left out and the cost of recognizing what a filed argument answers taken as fixed | Filed at the owner's request, from the rent-or-buy result of Karlin et al. 1988 ([THEORY-348](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-348.md)) set against [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s clause that recurrence is evidence of reuse, not the criterion. In [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s own terms the break-even rule needs no forecast and is worst-case optimal; [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md)'s second-occurrence rule is that rule when filing costs about one reconstruction. It does not reach staleness, which the theorem forbids rather than prices, or drifting costs, and where reuse can be forecast an expected-reuse rule can do better, so [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s criterion survives there. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-314](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-314.md) v2 | Reusing a filed argument has a recognition cost that a fixed per-use price leaves out: certifying that stored answers cover a new question is NP-complete even for conjunctive queries, grows with the number and size of the stored definitions rather than being a constant per item, and is undefined for an item filed without a statement of what it answers, so each filing raises the cost of later reuse and per-item break-even decisions are not independent | Filed at the owner's request, from the readings on answering queries using views (Levy, Mendelzon, Sagiv and Srivastava 1995; Chandra and Merlin 1977; Halevy 2001). [CLAIM-308](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md)'s guarantee needs a fixed, known per-use cost c_a; recognizing that a stored answer covers a new question is a search whose cost depends on everything stored, so filing one item changes the price of using the others. The hardness is worst case and over short definitions, partial reuse is cheap, and nothing here is measured on the record. | Proposed |

This half is scoped to the comparative-question paradigm. | [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md) v2 | A slowly changing collective variable, such as a reputation, a rivalry or a standing, is part of a collective's dynamics and not only an observer's average when its members read it, condition what they do on it, and by doing so regenerate it | A9 §3 and §10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, after Flack 2012 (LIT-1122, unread). | [CLAIM-329](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-329.md) v6 | A collective that replaces all its members persists, when it does, by causal transmission of the organization that produces it, not by resemblance: an organization of the same kind that arises independently is not its continuation, and a lapse in its coherence need not end it | A5, A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-16. A9 §9 separated three persistences that dissociate: state persistence (a variable changes slowly), dynamical persistence (characteristic responses continue) and historical persistence (the producing processes are transmitted and reconstituted across successive populations). It does not say what must be transmitted, or settle branching successors. | Proposed |

| [CLAIM-336](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-336.md) v9 | The pragmatic-transport and will-organization lines describe one model, an organization of operators that act on a shared interpretive state under a context while allocating one another's influence: a frame is the context under which operators act, a judgement is the response they yield, an action-generating regime is an operator or coalition, and a will-organization is the dynamics that allocates influence among them | The owner's, U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: the pragmatic-transport model and the will-organization model are "both manifestations of the same underlying model". The mapping is the assistant's, A6, filed at the owner's request ("address the still open stuff"). At U8 the owner endorsed it as filed ("Yes, as filed"). It reads both lines into [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s operator model. The sharp edge: it says the lines share one model, not that either line's results transfer to the other unchanged. Each mapping is a hypothesis until a result on one line is shown to hold, through it, on the other. Moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme on 2026-11-07 ([ADR-078](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-078.md)); the thesis is the owner's and the mapping the assistant's, as filed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-337](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md) v2 | Active inference already runs an internal loop: mental action selects among higher-level cognitive states and sets the precision of lower-level observations, structure learning reshapes the generative model without action, and a judgement is behaviour, so a judgement–observation loop may be action and perception one Markov blanket inward | The assistant's, A1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on active inference's behalf, strengthened at A4. Sandved-Smith et al. cast mental action as policy selection over higher-level cognitive states; Brouillet and Friston make felt fluency an inference about the precision of one's own processing; Smith et al. let a generative model grow its own structure by inference and learning alone. With Chalmers's point that judgements are behaviour, the owner's judgement is active inference's action relocated. What it does not reach: the diagram. A redescription with no action on the world concedes that action on the world is not part of the loop. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-338](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-338.md) v5 | The selectivity active inference gives action, sampling what one expects to experience, is played in the coupled meaning–authority model by the authority space: influence decides which operators retrieve and so what the next judgement observes, which makes Friston's self-confirming sampling the model's authority-to-interpretation arrow and his agent a coupled loop run without independent scoring | The owner's, U10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on Friston et al.'s "sampling selectively what one expects to experience": "I think this selectivity maps to the authority space in my coupled model." The sharp edge: the mapping relocates sampling from the world to retrieval, which is [CLAIM-337](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md)'s move reversed, and it holds only if the agent's own store can surprise it as the world can. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-355](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-355.md) v7 | In a distributed agent the binding of appraisal, readiness and governance into one response can be real while the single owner a self-model or collective self-description attributes it to is a representational construction, not a further entity; the illusion, where there is one, is in the attribution and belongs to whichever system adopts the representation, and this deflates the self without settling whether experience is real | The owner's, U26 and U27 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: at U26 whether, "adopting an illusionist/fictionalist position", the record can make claims about subjecthood; at U27, "illusory binding-type phenomena in distributed agents", starting from the record's emotion material. A26 answered with a selective fictionalism, "the imagined substantial owner, not the organized agent"; A27 located it: "The illusion might concern the owner, not the binding", and an illusion requires "which system constructs or adopts the misleading representation". The two are filed as one claim. It rests on no claim: the organizational-affect claim it would rest on, [CLAIM-039](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md), is Deferred, and whether that line reopens is the owner's decision, not made here. The sharp edge: it says nothing about whether the integrated state is felt. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-358](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-358.md) v4 | Learned local accommodation can reduce the amortized cost of recurrent arbitration: where a recurring conflict among an agent's processes admits a stable accommodation, settling it among the processes can cost less over repeated encounters than escalating each instance to a higher-level process that mediates or overrides, though local negotiation and the relations it needs are not free | The owner's, U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "processes which can navigate disagreement amongst themselves require fewer resources from the system than processes which need to activate additional subsystems to resolve disagreement." A45 put it in conditional form: where a recurring conflict admits a stable local accommodation, learning it amortizes the cost of higher-order mediation. It refines [CLAIM-261](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-261.md)'s "pays for its unity in effort": the divided agent pays for escalation. The sharp edge: it does not say local settlement is always cheaper, that an integrated agent works less hard, or anything about authenticity. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-362](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-362.md) | Non-domination of an agent's subcomponents is a candidate constituent of authenticity as an organizational achievement, not a sufficient criterion of ownership: higher-level processes need not impose the outcome because the lower-level ones already support it or settle their disagreement among themselves, and a process that rarely decides keeps access to the roles in which it is consequential | The owner's, U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "'authenticity' should be treated as an organizational achievement characterized by non-domination of subcomponents". | [CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md) v4 | Whether a training-time regulatory condition belongs to a network depends on which unit is individuated for the training dynamics and whose jurisdiction governs the updates; in conventional training most of that governance falls to the optimizer–model–data system, so a condition of training is not thereby a condition of the network | The owner's correction, U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "it might help clarify things if we apply our individuation and volition frameworks to this system", the system being a deep network during training (U30). | [CLAIM-393](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-393.md) | Ordinary and legal attributions of agency to an artifact cannot serve as the independent marks that would defeat the record's agency test, because they turn on whether its mechanism is understood: a known mechanism invites "This is all just programmed!", an inscrutable one invites fear, whatever the description lengths | From Boyle's "inscrutability paradox" in The Line ([LIT-1288](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1288.md), read in [NOTE-1014](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1014.md)): if an apparently general AI comes from well-understood programming, people will doubt it has autonomous consciousness, since it is "merely doing or saying that which we have programmed it to do"; if its workings are inscrutable, they will find it "more mysterious and potentially more threatening" (p. 30; pp. 54, 246, 272). [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md)'s defeater counts a test-passing factor that is "by independent marks, not an agent". The objection does not say [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md)'s test is wrong, only that this route to defeating it is not open. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-396](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-396.md) v2 | Directional information measures between reciprocally coupled units follow the path of a one-sided drive rather than the symmetry of the coupling, so the observed direction of information flow does not by itself reveal which way, or whether both ways, the units are coupled | The record's generalization of one study (Das, Manikandan and Banerjee, [THEORY-275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-275.md)) beyond its system, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 as the record's own claim, since the source makes no general claim. | [CLAIM-412](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md) v9 | Experience is constituted by interpretive organization, not produced by it: an appropriately organized process in which signals acquire significance for a system is the experience, so whether a system can have experience becomes whether it can sustain that organization | The owner's, U1 and U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-21. | [CLAIM-415](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-415.md) v5 | A person can be organized by a judgement they attribute to a collective that does not hold it: the audience in a self-model can be a false unity, and a judgement can shape a person who rejects it, because resisting it makes it consequential | From the owner's U39 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: how an individual's perspective is shaped by "the perception of a plurality of opinion where one may not exist (e.g. because of a loud minority)", and the phrase "I am whatever you say I am". A39: "An individual's perspective can be reorganized by what they believe other people's perspectives are—even when those other perspectives have been misperceived or scarcely exist." The edge: the attributed collective attitude itself is already held (List's falsely attributed common attitudes, [CASE-104](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-104.md)); what is new is its place in a person's own organization. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-417](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-417.md) v4 | What the record explained by "self" in its dispositional, persisting, self-governing and integrated senses is better explained by organizational perspectives, with a perspective, its carriers, its lineage and its representations kept apart; the subject sense stays a separate question, and narrative, presented and modeled selves involve representations that may describe a perspective, attribute it to a bearer or construct an owner, none of them the perspective itself | The owner's, at U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the record's earlier "selves" are "better described as 'organizational perspectives'". The sharp edge is what the replacement must keep apart: a perspective as realized, in one carrier or distributed across several, a recognizable character shared by many, a causal lineage of realizations, and representations of any of these. The exchange ran these together; the claim does not. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-423](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-423.md) v3 | In a political collective, components that change at different speeds (attention, coalitions, elected terms, administrative careers, law and treaties, generational memory) are not only nested by timescale: under a given institutional arrangement their different temporal horizons affect which forms of influence each can accumulate, exercise and keep, and so which of them holds authority over the others, so a state can stay continuous as an actor while the organization producing its positions changes under it | The owner's, at U28 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: domestic and international politics as the domain where "regime ecology" becomes concrete, with "separation of timescales in elections, durations of tenure in elected and appointed positions, lifespan, generational memory, etc." creating "amorphous collectives of varying orders and degrees of coupling". A28 stated the claim in its strongest line. It rests on [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md), that higher-level variables are characteristically slower, and denies that slowness alone settles which level governs. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-425](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md) v2 | A perspective governs itself with respect to social judgement to the extent that it keeps access to others' judgements of it while making their authority over its conduct depend on their grounds, not on their visibility, repetition or attributed plurality; neither absorbing every judgement nor resisting every one meets this, since both let the judgements set the terms of response | A39's closing thesis and its fourth reading of "I am whatever you say I am", in the exchange of 2026-10-22, filed at the owner's request. | [CLAIM-426](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-426.md) v2 | Where a judgement's circulation helps bring about what it says, its visibility, repetition and attributed plurality are evidence about what it will bring about, so the rule that a judgement's authority should come from its grounds and not its visibility holds for judgements of what already is, and not without qualification for judgements of what someone or something will become | The owner, on 2026-10-23, after [CLAIM-425](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md) was filed: "this is reminding me of 'hyperstition'". Land's definition ([LIT-1396](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1396.md)): "hyperstitions – by their very existence as ideas – function causally to bring about their own reality." [CLAIM-425](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md) says not to let a judgement's popularity substitute for its credibility. | [CLAIM-428](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-428.md) | Material interdependence couples parties' outcomes without fixing the perspective that organizes the coupling: the same dependence can be organized as mutual opportunity, as competitive vulnerability or as coercive leverage, so interdependence makes for peace to the extent that cooperation also changes which interests the parties' institutions recognize and who holds influence over them, and payoff coupling alone does not settle which | From the exchange of 2026-10-22, "Ben Franklin Effect Explained": the owner's U6, "maybe this is a stretch, but this seems like it could be connected to the hypothesis that trade promotes peace by coupling interests through coupled economies". | [CLAIM-430](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-430.md) | An interaction can make available a way of relating that its participants' operative perspectives did not hold, by giving each a role to enact in it, so that taking part can come before, and help produce, the reinterpretation it later seems to express; whether the change stays with the partner, generalizes to a category, or is reproduced beyond the encounter are further questions | From the exchange of 2026-10-22, "Ben Franklin Effect Explained": the owner's U2, asking for Franklin's favour to be read as a "perspectival invitation", and U4, connecting it to intergroup contact. | [CLAIM-431](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-431.md) v3 | A corporation's functional remorse cannot be told from prudence: any procedure or role duty that makes others' harms its concern was put there for its own ends, reputation, liability or recruitment, so the line between harm as concern and harm as threat, and with it the line between a remorseful and a psychopathic corporation, does not hold, and the clinical word adds nothing to a description of its incentives | The objection to the record's reading of the "institutional psychopath", revised on 2026-10-23 when the reading was revised. Velasquez's "as if" ([LIT-1432](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1432.md)) in functional form. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-432](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-432.md) v4 | A corporation can be an agent fit to be held responsible and the bearer of functional affect in Frijda's sense, so psychopathy's affective features can be assigned to it as well as its conduct: it lacks remorse, functionally, when harm it does to others is not among the concerns its own appraisals track and gains precedence over what it does only when a regulator or a market turns it into a threat to the corporation's concerns; that profile, threat without remorse, is the construct's, and it is changed by redesigning the corporation's concerns, not its members' characters | The record's reading of Bakan's "institutional psychopath" (LIT-1430, unread), filed at the owner's request on 2026-10-23 and revised the same day when the owner pointed out that the record's framework assigns affect to corporation-like things ([CLAIM-039](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md), reopened). On Frijda's account an emotion is an appraisal of an event's pertinence to a concern, eliciting action readiness with control precedence; a corporation has concerns, appraisals and readiness. A harm to others reaches its decisions either as one of its own concerns (procedures, role duties: functional concern and remorse) or as a threat to its other concerns (regulators, markets: functional fear). A corporation with only the second is functionally psychopathic across the construct, not in part. Wells Fargo's sales practices ([CASE-151](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-151.md)) are its documented case. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-433](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-433.md) v2 | The potential account of valence is an account of goal-conduciveness valence, not of intrinsic pleasantness: on the component process model's separation of levels of valence, the ordering that prevails ranks states by need satisfaction and goal attainment, the potential's strength tracks 'wanting' and its sign tracks goal conduciveness, while 'liking' is a separate appraisal with its own ordering; so the wanting–liking dissociation is two valence systems coming apart, as that separation predicts, and the objection that the account is not about pleasure is conceded rather than answered | The reply the owner asked for, 2026-10-23, to the objection that potential tracks 'wanting', not 'liking' ([CLAIM-438](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-438.md)). Shuman, Sander and Scherer's "levels of valence" separate intrinsic pleasantness from goal conduciveness, on Berridge's evidence; Scherer and Moors report that the two have different physiological signatures and combine multiplicatively. The record's ordering is goal conduciveness. The objection is conceded in a principled form: the account covers goal-conduciveness valence, and "hedonic" in the owner's thesis and its term now reads "goal-conduciveness", the owner having made that revision. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-435](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-435.md) v2 | Veit's common currency and ALARM's override are two regimes of one ordering serving as the negotiation's potential, compensatory and overriding, so their rivalry over what the first felt valence did becomes the question whether the earliest potential orderings are continuous: in motivational trade-off experiments, a continuous indifference curve between a noxious cost and a resource for Veit, a discontinuity at a threshold beyond which no resource buys the cost for ALARM; only a graded override, deciding at every level of its own intensity, lacks a currency altogether | A consequence of the owner's reframing of valence as ordering-potential ([CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md)). [THEORY-101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-101.md) records that its rivalry with ALARM "would dissolve if ALARM's "100% weight" were recast as a weight in a common currency rather than an override of it." It is recast instead: both are an ordering serving as the negotiation's potential, compensatory or overriding, and the trade-off test separates them by continuity. Corrected on reading Debreu before filing: a threshold override still has a (discontinuous) currency; only a graded override has none ([CLAIM-436](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-436.md), part 3a). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-437](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-437.md) v3 | 'Wanting' and 'liking' are saliences relative to different, overlapping processes, pursuit and consummation, each ranking states by their bearing on its own concerns; valence is then relative to a perspective, every perspective in the negotiation has its own, the system's valence is that of the perspective whose ordering is the negotiation's potential, and ambivalence is strong saliences of opposite sign with no potential absorbing them | The owner's, 2026-10-23: "maybe 'wanting' and 'liking' can be differentiated by characterizing them as saliencies relative to different (possibly overlapping) processes? I'm not sure if this resolves anything, but I think it least positions the wanting-liking distinction closer to the record's account." Worked through the same day. It relativizes valence to perspectives, as Shuman, Sander and Scherer's micro-valences already do, makes the system's valence the prevailing perspective's, and answers two problems the readings of incentive sensitization left open. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-438](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-438.md) v4 | An ordering serving as the negotiation's potential, as the potential account of valence defines it, tracks 'wanting', not 'liking': sensitized incentive salience wins a system's conflicts, persists and resumes while hedonic impact measured by taste reactivity stays flat or falls, so the regime the account calls hedonic valence is motivational valence, and hedonic valence, if it is anywhere in the account, is elsewhere | Raised by the reading of Berridge and Kringelbach ([NOTE-1110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1110.md)) filed on 2026-10-23 for the potential account. Sensitized 'wanting' meets all three of Frijda's marks of control precedence, which [TERM-076](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-076.md) uses to define potential, while 'liking' stays flat or falls. That is [CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md)'s own defeater, intensity that does not track control precedence. Hesp et al. ([NOTE-1111](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1111.md)) concede the same of their account, which puts valence in the system's model of its own potential rather than in the potential. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-439](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-439.md) v3 | A regime of valence is felt, in the sense of attended and available to the system's other processes, when the system that is in it also models it: when a deeper process infers which ordering wins its negotiation, which way the system is moving along it and how strongly it prevails, and the inference is used elsewhere in the system; unfelt valence is the potential without that model, as unfelt fluency is a change in precision without the inference about it | Filed at the owner's direction, 2026-10-23, as a candidate for when the functional regime of [CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md) is felt. It extends Brouillet and Friston's distinction ([THEORY-662](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-662.md)), unfelt fluency as a change in precision and felt fluency as a deeper inference about it, from fluency to valence, and Hesp et al.'s affective precision, a belief about how reliable one's own policies are. It is a candidate for [CLAIM-411](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-411.md)'s open sufficiency condition, for affect only, and it adopts [THEORY-662](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-662.md)'s sense of "felt": attended and available, not a further phenomenal fact. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md) v4 | An organization's appraisal is the negotiation among its perspectives, a common currency is that negotiation's admitting an ordering of the options it faces, and goal-conduciveness valence is a regime in which an ordering of the organization's own states by their bearing on its maintenance prevails in the negotiation; so valence presupposes contested rankings, not frustrated demands, its sign is whether the organization runs ahead of or behind a reference course along the potential ordering, its intensity is how far the negotiation's decisions follow that ordering, and ambivalence, where no ordering prevails, differs from neutrality, where one prevails and the organization keeps to its course | The owner's, 2026-10-23, in the discussion of [THEORY-101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-101.md) that followed the corporate psychopathy filing: "what if the 'appraisal' is the process by which competing perspectives negotiate amongst themselves? I think our earlier results equip us to reframe 'common currency' as 'admits an (at least instantaneous) ordering'. we could then formalize a hedonic valence as a circumstance in which a particular kind of ordering dominates the dynamics." Worked through the same day: potential read through Frijda's marks of control precedence, the kind of ordering fixed as one over the system's own states, and five consequences drawn. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-441](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-441.md) v3 | Flow tells against the potential account's condition that valence is undefined where no pair is contested: on the record's own account of flow nothing is overridden because an activity's immediate reward and its longer-run value coincide, yet flow is reported as positive, so either flow's positivity is intrinsic pleasantness and not goal-conduciveness valence, or flow keeps contested pairs its processes settle among themselves, or the positivity comes after the episode and not during it, or the condition is wrong | The assistant's, from the comparison of the record's will and affect lines of 2026-10-23, filed at the owner's direction. [CLAIM-162](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md) explains flow as intrapersonal synchronization in [TERM-050](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-050.md)'s sense: valuations coincide, so nothing needs overriding. [TERM-076](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-076.md) makes goal-conduciveness valence undefined where no pair is contested. Together they make flow's valence undefined, while flow is reported as positive. The report is second-hand: the flow literature is registered unread ([LIT-914](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-914.md)), and that it is positive during the episode, rather than in retrospect, is exactly what is unchecked. Four exits are named; the objection holds until one is shown. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-442](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-442.md) v4 | Frijda's emotion and the potential account's system valence sit on opposite sides of the gap between the precedence a motive claims and the authority it is granted: an emotion, action readiness claiming control precedence, is a claim, a perspective's valence is read on its claims, and the system's valence is read on what the negotiation grants, so a change in grants with the claims fixed, as mindfulness is said to make, changes the system's valence and leaves the perspectives' emotions and valences as they were | The assistant's, from a comparison of the record's will and affect lines made at the owner's request on 2026-10-23 and filed at the owner's direction. [CLAIM-283](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-283.md) splits precedence into what a motive claims and what it is granted. Frijda's emotion ([THEORY-055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md)) is on the claim side; the potential account ([CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md), [TERM-076](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-076.md)) reads valence off grants, the conflicts actually won. The claim resolves the asymmetry by [CLAIM-437](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-437.md)'s relativity: a perspective's valence is on the claim side, the system's on the grant side. The sharp edge: on this reading suspension changes the system's valence and no perspective's, which is what the mindfulness case must show. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-445](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-445.md) v3 | A protective regime, in a person, an institution or a system of states, becomes self-maintaining when the interventions it authorizes shift the evidence used to judge its necessity, the authority and resources of those who judge it, the capacities of its constituents or the threat environment itself in ways that favour its continuation; this can happen when the original threat was real and the first protection apt, and it is a failure only where the regime has become less responsive to evidence that it is no longer needed | The owner's, 2026-10-23, on the account of governance-maintained anxiety ([CLAIM-446](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-446.md)): "this seems like it would also be supported political and social scientific observations about state/societal protectionism". Worked through the same day (workbench entry of 2026-10-24, U16) with securitization, policy feedback, emergency powers and the security dilemma. The literatures support components of the mechanism; none shows a single self-confirming loop behind every protective policy. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-446](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-446.md) v7 | Some persistent anxiety may be governance-maintained rather than belief-maintained: anticipated threat grants defensive processes authority over action, attention and evidence acquisition; under the avoidance that authority selects, the hypotheses that the situation is dangerous and that it is safe predict the same observation, so repeated safety need not correct the threat estimate; relief reinforces the defense without being evidence of danger; and the regime can outlast a corrected belief, its pathology, where present, being defensive authority insensitive to corrective evidence at avoidable cost | The owner's, 2026-10-23, quoting "A governance prior can become self-protecting by reducing the access of the processes most likely to provide evidence against it": "I think you may have inadvertently landed on a formalization of anxiety". | [CLAIM-447](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-447.md) v2 | Model-based wanting is a pursuit process's ranking of the futures it predicts under candidate interventions, P(S \| do(a)) against P(S \| do(a₀)), while cue-triggered wanting is learned salience that need not compute those futures; a process's causal model, its wanting and its practical efficacy are separable, so learning to want differently, learning that a want will not pay, and learning not to act on it are three different changes | The owner's, 2026-10-23, asking what the record's account of wanting is: "i just found myself characterizing it as a kind of a prediction about a future state, and realized that really this is a do() operation and the future state that's being anticipated is what might or might not happen given a candidate intervention." | [CLAIM-451](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-451.md) v3 | When an organization's record of winning moves cycles, the failure is organizational nonintegrability, distinct from a perspective's own preference instability and from switching of the governing regime; it becomes organizational tension only when realized as costly reversal against demands the organization maintains, and cognitive dissonance only when that tension is detected and appraised as aversive; learning can relieve it by accommodation, by entrenched precedence or by cheap periodic coordination, which observed coherence does not tell apart, and ambivalence and nonintegrability entail neither one another | The owner's, 2026-10-23, quoting "A potential exists exactly when the finite relation of observed wins is acyclic": "rather than asserting potentials always have to exist, could we characterize cycles as a kind of internal tension or cognitive dissonance? preference/perspective/will instability?" | [CLAIM-468](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-468.md) v3 | Valence intensity need not be the strength of the prevailing ordering's potential: in Hesp et al.'s model negative valence is a weakening of the preference ordering's precision with a fall back to habit, and positive affect is reported to lower a goal's priority, so for either sign stronger valence can go with a weaker hold of the ordering | The difficulty [CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md)'s third clause records against itself ("The clause is open for both signs"), filed as an objection. | [CLAIM-490](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-490.md) | A fanbase is a mixture of spectators who relate to the club in different ways, as supporters, followers, fans and flâneurs, so the public stance credited to it is weighted towards the most committed types before any bias in who is sampled | From Giulianotti's taxonomy ([THEORY-1111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1111.md)): supporters are hot and bound to the club as community, while flâneurs are cool consumers who switch clubs. | [CLAIM-514](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md) | World-modeling is a family of resource-bounded capabilities for producing and using predictions about an environment's possibilities and consequences, each relative to a declared family of questions; a world model in the representational sense is one possible realization of them, competent behaviour can determine environmental structure without identifying any internal mechanism, and producing, maintaining and revising world-modeling capabilities are further achievements, not prerequisites of agency in general | The owner's preferred formulation at the second review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). | [CLAIM-519](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md) v2 | Competent behaviour does not establish an internal world model: over a fixed interface and a finite horizon, an agent with no model, whose actions are looked up from the history so far, reproduces the interaction distribution of an agent that has one exactly; a policy can identify predictive structure without any particular internal component realizing it, so compression and generalization support comparing candidate architectures, and establishing an internal mechanism needs evidence that discriminates candidate implementations, such as targeted interventions | The owner's thesis at U20 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): that under the record's framework a world model is "essentially a 'folk' explanatory tool and that no such thing need explicitly be present for the external behavior to be indistinguishable from a comparable black box agent which actually did contain a world model". | [CLAIM-527](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-527.md) v2 | Viable reach, valence and emotion are three quantities in an organization, not one: an emotion is a claim to precedence, system valence is movement along the ordering that wins the negotiation, and a change in what the organization can viably reach is neither, so an organization can run ahead along its prevailing ordering while its viable reach contracts | Filed 2026-10-31 from the readings of Massumi and McKim (2009) and Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024). Massumi's affect is a transition in a body's capacitation, augmented or diminished, and the parent paper defines agency as its augmenting half. | [CLAIM-541](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-541.md) v2 | Wu-wei is better read as control placed and timed where a system's own dynamics do most of the work than as the absence of control: Ott–Grebogi–Yorke control of chaos is a formal instance, in which small perturbations timed by the system's own wandering hold it on an unstable orbit, and the control, though small, continues for as long as the orbit is held; so reported effortlessness has at least three distinct sources, no conflict to override, conflict settled cheaply by learned accommodation, and conflict met as it arises by small well-timed feedback, which may feel alike and differ in mechanism | The owner's U17 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), quoting A16 on Ott–Grebogi–Yorke control: "that's very wu-wei". | [CLAIM-544](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-544.md) v4 | If a willed agent is the jurisdiction of its will-organization, then governing one's own governability is in part governing one's own individuation, in the constitutive sense of individuation at that level: a revision of the will-organization that changes which regimes it governs changes which willed agent there is, so a self-forming revision can be a re-individuation and not only a change in an agent's states, and whether the revised jurisdiction continues the earlier agent is a question of continuation, not of resemblance | The join the owner's U31 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02) asked for, "connect to individuation", made through the owner's own entry for it, [CLAIM-170](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-170.md), which A31 never cited. | [CLAIM-603](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) v4 | A capability lost because another reliably supplies it is the Black Queen's loss, favoured to the one who loses it, and whether it is dependency or division of labour is decided by the supply, not the loss: one-way supply set from outside, as aid is, leaves a dependence that nothing in the dependent's dynamics limits and that withdrawal punishes, while reciprocal loss, each partner supplying what the other gave up, leaves interdependence, so the aim framed as self-sufficiency is better framed as reciprocity | The assistant's, on the owner's remark of 2026-11-05 that "assured help makes recipients lose skill" sounds "closely related to niche differentiation and specialization phenomena". The record holds the biology. On the Black Queen Hypothesis ([THEORY-1048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md)) a cell that stops making a leaky public good saves its cost while others still supply it, so the loss is favoured to the individual and spreads. Buchnera ([THEORY-1103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md)) has lost the genes its host covers and kept those its host lacks. The Samaritan's dilemma has the same logic (Ostrom et al.), and Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's recipient is better off in the high-aid state. The loss itself is not the pathology. What differs is the supply. A Black Queen loss stops by itself when helpers grow rare, because the helpers are the same population. Aid is set from outside and does not fall as dependence grows, so nothing stops the loss short of what aid covers, and withdrawal returns the cost ([CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md)). Buchnera's loss runs both ways, and the result is interdependence. A state that taxes its citizens (Moore) is in the same position: it lost nothing, it exchanges. | [CLAIM-606](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md) v2 | A localized structure can persist by an internal balance that needs no supply, by a balance of gain and loss that needs a standing supply, or by a topological charge that continuous change cannot remove, and the three differ in what carries the structure's identity, how it forms and how it ends; because thresholds and abrupt ends appear in all of them, even with no supply at all, only withdrawing the supply and measuring the outflow tells which route a structure is on | The assistant's, after the owner's hunch that "the physics/dynamics of soliton formation could be a valuable angle through which to consider some of our questions about individuation and persistence".   supply. They come in a family set by their initial data, and they keep

- Topological solitons carry a charge that continuous change cannot
  remove.

So records kept per capacity (rosters, training assessments, equipment availability, turnout times) fix only the marginals, which bound readiness by the Fréchet inequalities and do not identify it. A record can refute a required readiness through the weakest capacity, and can certify it only when the shortfalls sum within the margin; between those, only joint evidence decides.
